neuromuscular-junction.short: The synapse where a motor neuron's terminal meets a muscle fibre and passes the signal on by releasing acetylcholine.

acetylcholine.short: A neurotransmitter. It excites skeletal muscle at the neuromuscular junction and, released by the vagus nerve, slows the heart.

acetylcholinesterase.short: The enzyme in the synaptic gap that breaks acetylcholine down within milliseconds, ending each signal.

safety-factor.short: Transmitter released per nerve impulse divided by the amount needed to trigger a muscle action potential. About 3–5 in healthy adult mammals.

ec-coupling.short: The chain from a muscle action potential to contraction: T-tubules, voltage sensors, calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum, calcium binding to troponin.

motor-unit.short: One motor neuron plus all the muscle fibres it supplies. When the neuron fires, all its fibres contract.

size-principle.short: Motor units are recruited in order of motoneuron size: small, slow, fatigue-resistant units first, large, fast, forceful units last.

rate-coding.short: Grading muscle force by changing how often motor units fire action potentials, as opposed to how many units are recruited.

mvc.short: The most force a person can produce on purpose. Forces are often given as % MVC.

sympathetic.short: The branch of the autonomic nervous system that prepares the body for effort and stress: it speeds the heart through noradrenaline on β₁ receptors.

parasympathetic.short: The branch of the autonomic nervous system for rest and basal function; through the vagus nerve and acetylcholine it slows the heart.

vagal-tone.short: The steady braking of heart rate by the vagus nerve at rest. It keeps resting HR well below the heart's own pacemaker rate.

sa-node-pacemaker.short: The heart's own pacemaker in the right atrium. Left alone it fires about 100 times a minute; autonomic nerves speed or slow it.

rr-interval.short: The time between two heartbeats (from one R peak of the ECG to the next), in ms. HR (beats·min⁻¹) = 60,000 ÷ RR.

hrv.short: The beat-to-beat variation in RR intervals. Short-term HRV mostly reflects vagal (parasympathetic) activity.

rmssd.short: Root mean square of successive RR differences: square each beat-to-beat difference, average them, take the square root. The main time-domain index of vagal HRV.
